quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #11
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What should you do when you approach a railroad crossing with no traffic signals?

options.text: Always come to a complete stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop.
All railroad crossings have signals, so this will never happen.
Speed up to cross the tracks quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Slow down when you see an unmarked railroad crossing. Look and listen for trains from both directions on all tracks before crossing. If you see or hear a train, stop at a safe distance and wait until it passes.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Watch for bicycles.
Bicycles are not allowed.
Bicycle repair shop ahead.
Bicycles have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for bicycles.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that bicycles may be in the area ahead.

questions.question: The traffic light turns yellow as you near an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get through before the red light.
Brake hard to stop.
Be ready to stop in the middle of the intersection.
Be ready to stop before you reach the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop before you reach the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the red light is coming soon. Get ready to stop safely before you enter the intersection.

questions.question: Two vehicles reach an intersection at the same time with no signs or signals. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The vehicle coming from the right.
The vehicle coming from the left.
The driver who honks first.
The vehicle traveling fastest.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle coming from the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no traffic control device, the vehicle approaching from the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: Two solid white lines across a traffic lane mark a crosswalk. As a driver, you should know:

options.text: Cars have the right-of-way over pedestrians in crosswalks.
Pedestrians in crosswalks have the right-of-way.
No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.
Pedestrians must stay out of the way of all traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrians in crosswalks have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Crosswalk lines mark safe places for people to cross roads. You must always stop for pedestrians in a crosswalk.

questions.question: When can you pass on the shoulder of the road?

options.text: When the car in front is turning.
When the car in front is going too slow.
When there are no pedestrians nearby.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: You cannot drive off the pavement or onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: What colors are highway exit distance signs?

options.text: Yellow with black letters.
Black with white letters.
Red with white letters.
Green with white letters.

questions.correctAnswerText: Green with white letters.
questions.explanation: Destination signs are green with white letters or symbols.

questions.question: When should you signal before passing another vehicle?

options.text: Just before changing lanes.
At any time.
After changing lanes.
Early enough so other drivers know your plans.

questions.correctAnswerText: Early enough so other drivers know your plans.
questions.explanation: Signal before passing so other drivers know what you plan to do in advance.

questions.question: What is the "No zone"?

options.text: The blind spots around a truck or bus.
A special speed zone.
A roadway with rules about stereo volume.
A television show that replaced The Twilight Zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The blind spots around a truck or bus.
questions.explanation: Trucks and buses have blind spots on the sides, rear, and front where cars cannot be seen. These are called the "No zone."

questions.question: When an officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, drivers should:

options.text: Follow the traffic light.
Follow the officer's directions.
Honk at the officer.
Watch what other cars are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the officer's directions.
questions.explanation: When an officer is directing traffic, follow the officer's directions instead of the traffic light.

questions.question: When a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light, who must yield?

options.text: Whoever started moving last
The driver
Whoever is slower
The pedestrian

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing at any intersection without a traffic light, with or without a crosswalk.

questions.question: What does a single dashed yellow line mean?

options.text: Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.
Both lanes travel in the same direction.
Drivers may not pass.
Drivers may pass, even if it could be dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A single dashed yellow line means traffic moves in opposite directions. Drivers can pass only if it is safe and they will not interfere with oncoming traffic.

questions.question: If you are stranded in a snowstorm, what should you do?

options.text: Get out of the car and go for help.
Lay down in your car and go to sleep.
Walk into the road and get the attention of other drivers.
Stay in the car, as you are most likely to be found when you stay in your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the car, as you are most likely to be found when you stay in your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Stay in your car and wait for help. You are more likely to be found if you stay in your vehicle. Walking in a snowstorm is dangerous.

questions.question: When may you turn right on red?

options.text: After coming to a complete stop and yielding to pedestrians and vehicles in the intersection.
Before pedestrians have crossed any intersecting crosswalks.
Where there is a sign prohibiting turning right on red.
Before coming to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: After coming to a complete stop and yielding to pedestrians and vehicles in the intersection.
questions.explanation: You may turn right on red only after coming to a full stop. Make sure it is safe and there is no sign prohibiting the turn. Always watch for pedestrians.

questions.question: Which statement about winter driving is false?

options.text: Winter is the most difficult driving season.
Checking your vehicle's antifreeze and windshield washer fluid levels is especially important during the winter.
Using cruise control in winter weather is a safe thing to do.
It is best to use snow tires on your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using cruise control in winter weather is a safe thing to do.
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control in snow, rain, fog, or other hazardous conditions. Winter requires extra caution. Check antifreeze and windshield washer fluid regularly. Snow tires improve traction on slippery roads.

questions.question: What is the purpose of highway markings?

options.text: Are usually not important.
Are only found in construction zones.
Provide information for drivers.
Are usually red and blue in color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provide information for drivers.
questions.explanation: Highway markings provide information to drivers. They help position vehicles correctly, show safe passing zones, and warn drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: What does a speed restriction sign show?

options.text: May be ignored in rainy, snowy, or icy conditions.
Has a triangular shape.
Is blue with black lettering.
Shows a recommended speed for a curve or turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shows a recommended speed for a curve or turn.
questions.explanation: Speed restriction signs show a recommended speed for curves and turns. Even if you feel safe driving faster in good weather, always slow down in rain, snow, or ice.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing red traffic light?

options.text: Drive through the intersection if there is no crossing traffic.
Continue driving, as they have the right-of-way.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat the light like a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat the light like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights warn of dangerous intersections. Treat them as stop signs.

questions.question: What is your blind spot?

options.text: You cannot see without moving your head.
Directly behind your vehicle.
You see in your rearview mirror.
You see in your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see without moving your head.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see without turning your head. They are located to the sides and behind your vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Stop and wait for the light to change.
Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.
Drive carefully through the intersection.
Prepare to stop; the light is about to turn red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive carefully through the intersection.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and be cautious. Look both ways for traffic before proceeding through the intersection.

questions.question: If you pass your exit on the interstate, what should you do?

options.text: Cut quickly across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.
Keep driving and use the next exit.
Put your vehicle in reverse to go back to the exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep driving and use the next exit.
questions.explanation: Don't make a sudden turn at your exit. If you miss your exit, drive to the next one.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Slam on your brakes.
Hold the steering wheel tight and slowly come to a stop.
Keep driving normally.
Turn on your flashers and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel tight and slowly come to a stop.
questions.explanation: Don't brake suddenly. Grip the steering wheel firmly to stay in your lane. Slow down gradually by easing off the gas. Once you're going very slowly, brake lightly and pull to a safe area.

questions.question: What happens when you drink alcohol while taking drugs?

options.text: The effects of the drugs and alcohol decrease.
The effects of the drugs and alcohol increase.
It helps cure your illness.
It improves your driving ability.

questions.correctAnswerText: The effects of the drugs and alcohol increase.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol and drugs increases the effects of both. Driving is unsafe after using alcohol or drugs alone, and even more dangerous when you mix them.

questions.question: You see an oncoming car to your left and a bicyclist to your right. What should you do?

options.text: Pull onto the shoulder.
Go between both of them.
Let the car pass first, then pass the bicycle.
Pass the bicycle quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the car pass first, then pass the bicycle.
questions.explanation: Handle one hazard at a time. Don't try to squeeze between multiple hazards. Let the oncoming car pass, then pass the bicyclist.

questions.question: What is the most important thing to remember about speed on curves?

options.text: Drive at the speed limit entering the curve, then slow down at the sharpest part.
Slow down before you enter the curve.
Speed up gently before you enter the curve.
Drive at the speed limit before, during, and after the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve. Your vehicle's inertia makes turning harder. Reducing speed before the curve helps you stay in control.

questions.question: What should you do before turning?

options.text: Use your signal.
Turn the wheel.
Speed up.
Change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your signal.
questions.explanation: Activate your turn signal 3 to 4 seconds before you turn.

questions.question: A driver's left arm and hand point downward. What does this mean?

options.text: Turn left.
Turn right.
Stop.
Start moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: A left arm and hand pointing downward means the driver plans to stop. Adjust your driving if you are following this car.

questions.question: When turning left onto a one-way street, which lane should you turn into?

options.text: The right lane.
The lane closest to your previous lane.
Either lane.
Neither lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to your previous lane.
questions.explanation: Always turn into the lane closest to where you came from.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Traffic signal ahead.
Fire station.
T intersection.
Left turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This yellow sign with black markings warns you of an upcoming traffic signal. Be ready to respond to red, yellow, and green lights and watch for cross traffic.

questions.question: When should you NOT pass another vehicle?

options.text: On a hill or curve.
When a school bus has flashing red lights.
When approaching an intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Never pass on hills, curves, at intersections, on railroad crossings, on bridges, or in no passing zones. Never pass a school bus with flashing red lights unless you're on the opposite side of a road with a median or center turn lane.

questions.question: If a tire blows out while you are driving, what should you do?

options.text: Brake hard right away.
Keep the car straight and slow down by releasing the gas pedal.
Keep your current speed and steer straight.
Swerve back and forth to warn drivers behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the car straight and slow down by releasing the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, hold the steering wheel firmly and keep the car going straight. Take your foot off the gas pedal slowly. Do not brake until you have control. Once the car is steady, brake gently and move to the side of the road safely.

questions.question: When passing on a multilane highway, what should you do?

options.text: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
Pass only on the right.
Watch for oncoming traffic.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before you pass, check that the passing lane is clear. Give the proper turn signal to show you are changing lanes.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is illegal to drive around lowered gates at a crossing.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger tells you to.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing red lights and gates.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger, stop sign, or warning devices like gates or flashing lights tell you to. Not all crossings have these devices. It is illegal to drive around lowered railroad gates.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic light works the same way as which sign?

options.text: A slow sign.
A yield sign.
A stop sign.
An intersection sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign.
questions.explanation: When you see a flashing red light, you must stop and let all other traffic that does not have to stop go first.

questions.question: If you notice a vehicle problem that could affect safety, what should you do?

options.text: Fix the problem as soon as possible.
Fix the problem when you have money.
Drive slowly.
Drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix the problem as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Any vehicle problem that could affect safety must be fixed right away. Fix problems before you drive the vehicle.

questions.question: When can you carefully drive through a yellow light?

options.text: When an emergency vehicle is crossing your lane.
When pedestrians are crossing.
When you are turning right.
When you are already in the intersection as the light turns yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are already in the intersection as the light turns yellow.
questions.explanation: If the light turns yellow while you are already in the intersection, you can continue through carefully.

questions.question: What colors are used for warning signs?

options.text: Black letters or symbols on a white background.
Black letters or symbols on a yellow background.
White letters or symbols on a blue background.
White letters or symbols on a green background.

questions.correctAnswerText: Black letters or symbols on a yellow background.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black letters or symbols. Work zone warning signs are orange with black letters or symbols.

questions.question: Larger vehicles have:

options.text: Larger blind spots.
Smaller blind spots.
No blind spots.
The same blind spots as smaller vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Larger blind spots.
questions.explanation: Larger vehicles have bigger blind spots. Large trucks and SUVs have areas near the back that cannot be seen in side or rearview mirrors.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is approaching?

options.text: Try to reach your destination before it catches up.
Keep driving but try to stay out of its way.
Pull over to the side of the road and stop completely.
Stop in the middle of the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and stop completely.
questions.explanation: You must let all emergency vehicles with sirens or flashing red, blue, or white lights go first. Pull over to the right side of the road when possible. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first before pulling over.

questions.question: When exiting a highway, when should you slow down?

options.text: On the main road just before the exit lane.
Once you see a toll booth.
Once you have moved into the exit lane.
When you first see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Once you have moved into the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Move into the exit lane early. Do not slow down until after you have moved into the exit lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turns.
Right turns are allowed.
Stop before turning right.
Sharp curve ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turns.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a red slash means no. This sign prohibits right turns at this location.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what is important to do?

options.text: Signal before you change lanes.
Check your blind spot.
Make sure the lane is clear.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Make sure the lane is clear before you move.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The road ahead ends.
You must turn either right or left.
A four-way intersection is ahead.
A road joins from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must turn either right or left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a Y intersection ahead. You must choose to bear right or left.

questions.question: What happens if a bicyclist breaks traffic laws?

options.text: Bicyclists do not have to follow traffic laws.
They can be ticketed.
They will always get a warning.
Their bicycle will be taken away.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can be ticketed.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists must follow the same traffic laws as drivers. Both can be ticketed for breaking traffic laws.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Drive slowly and use your horn.
A bus stop is ahead.
You are entering a school parking lot.
A school zone is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A school zone is ahead.
questions.explanation: This yellow sign warns drivers about a school zone. Slow down and watch for children.

questions.question: Drivers cannot pass on either side of a ____ centerline.

options.text: Combination solid and broken yellow
Single broken yellow
Double solid yellow
Single broken white

questions.correctAnswerText: Double solid yellow
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line means no passing from either direction.

questions.question: Which of these does not happen after drinking alcohol?

options.text: Your reaction time slows down.
You misjudge speed and distance.
You become less alert.
You calm down and focus better.

questions.correctAnswerText: You calm down and focus better.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows reaction time, reduces vision, impairs judgment, and increases risk-taking. It does not help you calm down or concentrate.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving on a wet road?

options.text: Faster speeds make your tires less effective.
Good tires prevent water from affecting your car.
Deep water is safer than shallow water.
Slower speeds make the road more slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: Faster speeds make your tires less effective.
questions.explanation: As you go faster on wet roads, your tires cannot remove water as well. At high speeds, you may hydroplane and lose control.

questions.question: When should you allow extra space when stopping?

options.text: On an uphill slope.
At an intersection.
At a stop sign.
At a toll plaza.

questions.correctAnswerText: On an uphill slope.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space on an uphill slope. If the car ahead rolls backward, you will have room to avoid a collision.

questions.question: What does a "No standing" sign mean?

options.text: You cannot stop your vehicle there at any time.
You can park there if the driver stays in the vehicle.
You can stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.
You can stop to load or unload items.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.
questions.explanation: A "No standing" sign allows brief stops only to pick up or drop off passengers.
